_doc: Retail markup over book — the spread a used-car store lists at above what a unit is worth. Raised 10 points in the #286 calibration pass. The pre-#286 table (1.20-1.28) could not cover the cost basis it sat on: a store bought at roughly book, spent the condition tier's recon on top of that, and held a minimum front gross, which left the floor price ABOVE the asking price on most units — the deal was dead on price before the customer formed an opinion. Deliberately not raised further: the ask is what a walk-in has to afford, `pickVehicleForMatch` filters the lot by affordability before it ever looks at fit, and every extra point of markup shows up as customers walking on `no_fit` instead of on price. +0.10 is the measured peak of total cars sold — past it the close band keeps improving while the store sells fewer cars, because it is losing them at the door instead. The rest of the store's gross was found on the buy side (marketEconomy.motivatedSeller). Percentage spread is widest on the cheap end (economy) and narrowest on the expensive end (luxury), which is how the real market prices it.
